extracted.intended_audience: sovereigns, their principal ministers, and readers/students of political theology and philosophy
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying Hobbes's standards for (1) when and how revelation and scripture bind subjects, (2) how prophets and canonical books are to be recognized, and (3) required semantic precedents for theological-political reasoning in a Christian commonwealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereigns need only the science of natural justice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Science of Naturall Justice, is the onely Science necessary for Soveraigns, and their principall Ministers; they need not be charged with the Sciences Mathematicall, further, than by good Lawes to encourage men to the study of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sovereigns should focus on knowledge necessary to secure Peace and Justice; other sciences may be promoted by law but are not required for sovereign function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of Christian politiques: natural and prophetic word
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Nature and Rights of a CHRISTIAN COMMON-WEALTH... the ground of my Discourse must be, not only the Naturall Word of God, but also the Propheticall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When dealing with Christian polity, both natural reason (the natural word of God) and prophetic revelation are relevant; neither alone suffices to ground the whole discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not renounce senses and natural reason
rubrics_metrics.description: We are not to renounce our Senses, and Experience; nor (that which is the undoubted Word of God) our naturall Reason... they are the talents which he hath put into our hands to negotiate, till the coming again of our blessed Saviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faith and reason/sense should operate together: where scripture appears above reason, the fault is in interpretation or ratiocination, not in reason itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: When scripture is too hard: 'captivate the understanding' means submission of will, not intellect
rubrics_metrics.description: By the Captivity of our Understanding, is not meant a Submission of the Intellectual faculty, to the Opinion of any other man; but of the Will to Obedience, where obedience is due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a scriptural passage is beyond examination, one should 'captivate' (i.e., restrain) their understanding from contradiction and submit the will to lawful authority—trust and faith in the speaker—without pretending to acquire notions contrary to reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modes of divine speech and their evidentiary force
rubrics_metrics.description: When God speaketh to man, it must be either immediately; or by mediation of another man... To say he hath spoken to him in a Dream... or a Vision... or by supernaturall Inspiration... yet he obliges no man to beleeve he hath so done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private claims of dreams, visions, or inspiration have little force to oblige others to belief; only a sovereign (or recognised authoritative channel) can bind subjects to obedience arising from such claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of prophets: two marks (miracles and doctrinal conformity)
rubrics_metrics.description: There be two marks... One is the doing of miracles; the other is the not teaching any other Religion than that which is already established. Asunder... neither of these is sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both marks must coincide: miracles alone do not prove a prophet, nor does doctrinal conformity alone; their joint presence is required to acknowledge immediate revelation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miracles alone are insufficient and may be deceptive
rubrics_metrics.description: God wil not have miracles alone serve for arguments, to approve the Prophets calling... the works of the Egyptian Sorcerers, though not so great as those of Moses, yet were great miracles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because false prophets can exhibit marvels, miracles must not be the sole criterion; evaluate also by doctrine and political consequences (e.g., if miracles incite revolt treat them as trials of allegiance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prophecy predictions must be confirmed by events within a reasonable time
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Prophet shall have spoken in the name of the Lord, that which shall not come to passe, that’s the word which the Lord hath not spoken... the miracles that oblige us to beleeve a Prophet, ought to be confirmed by an immediate, or a not long deferr'd event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prophetic utterances should be verifiable by fulfillment; prophecies postponed beyond reasonable temporal verification are of little evidentiary value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miracles that call for revolt are not to be heeded
rubrics_metrics.description: How great soever the miracle be, yet if it tend to stir up revolt against the King... he that doth such miracle, is not to be considered otherwise than as sent to make triall of their allegiance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Miraculous signs advocating political rebellion should be treated politically (as tests of loyalty), not as legitimate divine mandates.

rubrics_metrics.name: When miracles cease, Scripture supplies their place as the standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeing therefore Miracles now cease, we have no sign left, whereby to acknowledge the pretended Revelations... nor obligation to give ear to any Doctrine, farther than it is conformable to the Holy Scriptures, which... supply the want of all other Prophecy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the absence of present miracles, the canonized Scriptures are the authoritative measure; private revelations without conformity to Scripture carry no binding force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical books are those established by sovereign/church authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Those Books only are Canonicall, that is, Law, in every nation, which are established for such by the Soveraign Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Canon status is not purely intrinsic to texts but depends on authoritative recognition by the sovereign (or the Church acting as sovereign in its domain).

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for dating/authorship: use internal textual markers
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles of Books are not arguments sufficient to prove authorship... phrases like 'unto this day' and references to other books/registers show that many biblical books were written after the events they describe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infer antiquity and authorship by internal evidence (linguistic forms, anachronistic phrases, cross-references to registers or later events) rather than relying solely on traditional titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Scripture: its end is to set forth the Rights of God's kingdom
rubrics_metrics.description: They conspire to one and the same end, which is the setting forth of the Rights of the Kingdome of God... the Histories and the Prophecies... the Gospels, and Epistles... have had one and the same scope, to convert men to the obedience of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand scriptural writings as having a unified political-theological purpose: inculcating obedience and delineating the rights/duties within the divine kingdom as manifested through different authorities (Moses, Christ, Apostles).

rubrics_metrics.name: When Scripture has legal authority: consonance with natural law or sovereign enactment
rubrics_metrics.description: As far as they differ not from the Laws of Nature, there is no doubt, but they are the Law of God... If they be made Law by God himselfe, they are of the nature of written Law, which are Laws to them only to whom God hath so sufficiently published them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scriptural precepts that align with natural reason carry self-evident authority; where they do not, their force as law depends on being promulgated or recognised by the legitimate legislative authority (the sovereign).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to obey Scripture depends on recognized public authority
rubrics_metrics.description: He... to whom God hath not supernaturally revealed, that they are his, nor that those that published them, were sent by him, is not obliged to obey them, by any Authority, but his, whose Commands have already the force of Laws; that is to say... the Soveraign, who only has the Legislative power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent private supernatural revelation, individuals are bound to Scripture as law only insofar as the political sovereign (or duly authorised church) incorporates/recognises it; private interpretation does not bind others.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Church as one person: collective authority and its limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Church be not one person, then it hath no authority at all; ... Now if the whole number of Christians be not contained in one Common-wealth, they are not one person; nor is there an Universall Church that hath any authority over them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims of universal ecclesiastical authority presuppose a single corporate person; without a universal commonwealth of Christians, universal church authority to make Scripture law is incoherent—authority devolves to each sovereign polity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreter authority: those with lawful power over a writing may approve its interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whosoever hath a lawfull power over any Writing, to make it Law, hath the power also to approve, or disapprove the interpretation of the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal/political authority that determines a text's force as law also controls authoritative interpretation within its jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fix meanings of ambiguous words before theological-political reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation of all true Ratiocination, is the constant Signification of words... It is necessary... to determine, out of the Bible, the meaning of such words, as by their ambiguity, may render what I am to inferre upon them, obscure, or disputable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before drawing normative conclusions from scripture, define key terms (e.g., 'body', 'spirit') as used in the text to avoid equivocation and faulty inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of 'body' and 'spirit' for scriptural usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Word Body... signifieth that which filleth, or occupyeth some certain room... In the common language of men, Aire, and Aeriall Substances... are called Wind, or Breath, or... Spirits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt clear operational definitions: 'body' as that which occupies space (substance), and 'spirit' as aerial or noncorporeal substances inferred by their effects; avoid conflating categories (e.g., 'incorporeall body').
